test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 10 March, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.**

He has been / told many a times to / mind his manners.
solution:
The erroneous part is: **told many a times to**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct phrase is "many times" without the indefinite article **"a"**.
 
• The phrase "many a" is used to emphasize singularity or uniqueness, as in "many a man" or "many a time."
 
• However, when discussing repetition or frequency, the correct phrase is simply "many times."

The corrected sentence would be: *He has been told **many times** to mind his manners.*
